title: 8 ferramentas para uma gestão de projetos eficiente
summary: Descubra 8 ferramentas gratuitas e eficientes para uma gestão de projetos e equipe mais organizada e produtiva. Aprimore suas habilidades organizacionais e alcance melhores resultados.
body_text: A tecnologia tem aumentado a eficácia dos projetos. 8 ferramentas para uma gestão de projetos eficiente. Como gestor, você reconhece a importância de aplicar conhecimentos, habilidades, técnicas e recursos no desenvolvimento de um projeto com o time. Sendo assim, ferramentas para gestão de projetos são bem-vindas. Afinal, organização e praticidade levam direto ao que importa e previnem o desgaste desnecessário. Softwares de gerenciamento aprimoram a coordenação do serviço, além de aumentarem a produtividade e a qualidade do trabalho da equipe. Às vezes, ferramentas simples, como bloco de notas virtual, já fazem uma grande diferença. Quando falamos de ferramentas para gestão de projetos, incluímos a gestão da equipe . Não se trata apenas de distribuir tarefas e alocar tempo. Conforme o tamanho do time e a natureza do projeto, é preciso combinar vários recursos. Neste post, vamos mostrar alguns desses recursos, a maioria gratuitos, e como você pode adotá-los na gestão da instituição de ensino . As 8 melhores ferramentas para gestão de projetos e equipe 1. Monday.com É uma ferramenta de gerenciamento de projetos e colaboração em várias plataformas. Com ela, você centraliza toda a comunicação e mantém as pessoas envolvidas e focadas no que importa. O Monday.com permite planejar e executar no mesmo local. Em vez de listar tarefas, o software facilita que todos visualizem o cenário geral. A ferramenta é fácil de usar, porque cria linguagem visual e ainda permite gerenciar qualquer coisa: projetos, tarefas, pessoas, campanhas publicitárias, CRM , projetos de clientes… 2. Slack É a melhor ferramenta para equipes que precisam se comunicar constantemente . Crie canais Slack e configure as notificações para aumentar a produtividade do pessoal. Assim, é possível obter uma visão mais ampla das tarefas e projetos em curso. O software permite bate-papo, é integrado ao Google Drive, Box ou Dropbox para o compartilhamento de arquivos. Além disso, configura lembretes e realça as palavras que devem ser notificadas. 3. Quire Com interface simples e fácil de usar, o aplicativo permite ver tarefas e subtarefas imediatamente, sem que você tenha de clicar especificamente em cada uma delas. Nele, os desafios são divididos passo a passo. Em suma, o Quire é um aplicativo de gerenciamento de tarefas moderno que ajuda as equipes a capturar idéias , seja via texto, câmera ou até mesmo através do aplicativo de assistente pessoal, a Siri. Isso pode ser feito a qualquer hora e de qualquer lugar. As tarefas são divididas em etapas de ação e rastreadas facilmente. 3. Teamwork Com esse programa, você estima o tempo necessário para concluir as tarefas e ainda registra o tempo real. Em pouco tempo, o time passa a estimar com precisão o tempo que cada tarefa leva para ser concluída. Em resumo, o Teamwork estima e rastreia o tempo gasto num projeto; oferece relatórios personalizados de tempo, com opções para exportar (para Gmail, OneDrive, Google Drive, Hubstaff). Finalmente, permite gerenciar projetos e ferramentas de colaboração para equipes de teste beta, como o Teamwork Chat. 4. Asana Combina elementos de gerenciamento de projetos, armazenamento de arquivos e colaboração. Além disso, ajuda a gerenciar projetos entre a equipe sem e-mail. O software permite dividir o trabalho em tarefas e atribuí-los entre os membros da equipe . Organizar tarefas, verificar o progresso da equipe, notificar sobre atualizações e mais! O layout é simples e recomendado para projetos pouco complexos e com equipe pequena. 5. Fleep Foi criado com a finalidade de melhorar a colaboração do projeto, facilitando a comunicação entre os envolvidos e agendando tarefas leves. O Fleep é para quem está exausto de inúmeras conversas por e-mail, que levam horas para serem concluídas. Entre os recursos, estão a possibilidade de comunicação entre envolvidos e parceiros, compatibilidade de e-mail (quem não é usuário, recebe e-mails comuns), fixação das mensagens importantes ao lado de cada diálogo. Ele também é integrado com Google Hangouts. A vantagem principal é que você nunca precisa sair da ferramenta para transmitir suas mensagens às outras pessoas , sejam elas usuárias ou não do Fleep. Afinal, o programa oferece um canal para colaboração contínua que engloba a si mesmo, e-mail e Hangouts do Google. 6. RescueTime O software rastreia exatamente como você e seus colaboradores gastam o tempo nos respectivos dispositivos digitais . Tudo que é feito é categorizado automaticamente para mensurar o tempo gasto em aplicativos, sites e projetos específicos. Desse modo, é possível avaliar a produtividade diária. O programa permite, ainda, entender onde você gasta o tempo em todos os seus dispositivos ; quais aplicativos e sites distraem mais; quanto tempo você gasta em reuniões, respondendo a e-mails e nas mídias sociais. Também mostra quando você é mais (e menos) produtivo a cada dia e como o uso do smartphone afeta sua capacidade de realizar um trabalho significativo. 7. Easy Projects Overview É uma plataforma de gerenciamento e colaboração de projetos para empresas de médio porte. Ela ajuda os departamentos de marketing, TI e operacional a substituir planilhas, e-mails e quadros por uma única ferramenta on-line. Permite ver o status dos projetos em tempo real, prevê a disponibilidade de recursos e mantém os funcionários engajados. Outros benefícios incluem: planejamento de recursos , portfólios de projetos, ferramentas de colaboração, orçamento do projeto, listas de tarefas pessoais e mais. Os projetos são divididos em tarefas, que por sua vez são atribuídas aos membros da equipe, com prazos e prioridade predefinidos. Utilidade e praticidade das ferramentas de gestão de projetos Como vimos anteriormente, as ferramentas de gestão de projetos ajudam o gestor a sistematizar e organizar melhor o trabalho, não apenas no planejamento, mas também no acompanhamento de progresso, gerenciamento de orçamento e o que mais for necessário. O mercado de softwares de gerenciamento de projetos é vasto. Basta escolher a ferramenta mais adequada às suas necessidades e fazer um a combinação eficiente. Várias delas são grátis ou pagas a partir de um certo número de recursos. Por isso, antes de se comprometer com um pacote, procure informar-se sobre a ferramenta e conhecer bem as reais necessidades de gestão da instituição . É importante mencionar que essas ferramentas não substituem a experiência e o treinamento profissiona l. Contudo, elas permitem aprimorar as habilidades organizacionais , investir tempo e recurso no que realmente importa e entender porque algo vai bem ou mal em cada projeto. Que tal fazer um teste? Se você gostou do artigo, leia também sobre como gerenciar uma equipe remotamente no blog da Quero Educação. Não deixe de assinar nossa newsletter e acompanhar os nossos conteúdos.

title: Truewind @ AICPA Engage 24
summary: > Last week, Truewind launched its AI-powered accounting platform for accounting firms at the AICPA Engage 24 Conference.
body_text: Last week, Truewind launched its AI-powered accounting platform for accounting firms at the AICPA Engage 24 Conference. We were a Silver Sponsor, and had the chance to showcase our new product to hundreds of people over the course of three days. Up until then, we worked quietly with our early design partners to rethink accounting software from the ground up with AI at its center. After months of engineering, we were ready to show the world what we had built. Below is a recap of our week at Engage 24, Las Vegas. Sunday June 9 - Setting Up 10 Truewind team members flew into Las Vegas from San Francisco, New York, Seattle, Dallas, Toronto and Brazil. For many, it was their first time meeting each other. This was also all our first time going to a conference as exhibitors. We spent the day preparing everything. We printed flyers, post cards and business cards introducing Truewind. Unpacked Truewind branded swag, coffee cups, and snacks. Everything at our booth would have the Truewind logo. A 13" Las Vegas themed photo wall & video wall introducing Truewind. Designed to give attendees a delightful, even fun experience with us. As newcomers to an established conference, we knew we would have to make a splash. And we did. Our island booth stood 13" with backlit logos so people could see our booth from across the exhibit hall. Monday June 10 - Game Day You know when you do a product launch and it's crickets on the other side? We went into this conference with that mindset - if no one comes by our booth, let's be proactive and go talk to people. We had the opposite problem. We had more traffic than we could handle. All 10 Truewinders were talking to prospects every minute of the day. We must've given over a hundred demos in that day alone. A partner from an accounting firm visited our booth and said: "When I see a well-designed booth experience like this, I can tell you care about the customer experience." That was our aim - to provide a delightful experience. Whether it was the booth, the video wall, the raffle prizes, the artisan coffee, or the specialty snacks, we wouldn't be able to figure out the attribution. It was probably all of the above. The energy around our booth was palpable. At the end of the day, everyone said "I need a drink." On day one, we learned that accountants are not shying away from AI. In fact, many of them are leaning in . We met CIOs and Partners-in-charge of CAS practices at several of the top 100 US public accounting firms. Many asked thoughtful questions, demonstrating that they've thought deeply about this technology. What specific accounting workflows does your product automate? What kind of data does the AI need to perform at its best, and how is this data processed? We do not have the luxury of being wrong. How do you handle the fact that LLMs hallucinate? Tuesday June 11 - Leading a Conference Session During a discussion we led, we emphasized that the next decade in accounting will be vastly different from the last, with generative AI leveling the competitive playing field. We explained how AI enables firms to achieve more with the same headcount, expedite month-end close processes, and provide strategic insights. title: Cómo romper el ciclo y sobrevivir al reclutamiento masivo
summary: Descubre cómo romper el ciclo de supervivencia al reclutamiento masivo con la automatización y la IA, así como lo hicieron Heineken, Oxxo y Nemak, mejorando la eficiencia, reduciendo costos y optimizando el tiempo de contratación.
body_text: Un día en reclutamiento masivo Otra semana transcurre en el cronograma del equipo de reclutamiento. La nómina continúa en un 40%, sin capacidad para completarla más rápido. Los reclutadores revisan las 200 solicitudes de candidatos, dedicando hasta dos horas diarias. Le siguen las llamadas, los recordatorios, los seguimientos y el alto porcentaje de ausencias a la primera entrevista. De los que se presentaron para la entrevista, algunos olvidaron su documentación, lo que lleva a enviarlos a casa y pedirles que regresen con sus documentos. Si regresan, con suerte todo estará en orden y podrás comenzar el proceso de contratación y onboarding. Te sientas en tu escritorio a preparar el informe sobre los KPIs del proceso de contratación para compartirlo con otros líderes. Miras a tus reclutadores, todos ocupados y sobrecargados con las tareas manuales de filtrado, programación, recordatorios y entrevistas. No hoy, no esta semana. Con suerte, el próximo mes será un mejor momento para aquellas mejoras que seguramente traerán valor. Sin embargo, todavía estás atascado en lo que es urgente en vez de lo que es importante. Problemas comunes en los equipos de RH Esta es la realidad para muchos equipos. La competencia por los trabajadores de primera línea ha aumentado, lo que dificulta llegar a los mejores candidatos lo suficientemente rápido. Los equipos agregan horas extras a su carga de trabajo y aún parecen llegar a los candidatos después de que la competencia ya les haya ofrecido un trabajo. Mientras tanto, los formularios de aplicación quedan vacíos porque prefieren optar por otra aplicación más sencilla. El problema no es solo no llegar a tus candidatos lo suficientemente rápido, sino también estresar y sobrecargar a tu equipo con trabajo manual innecesario. Esto desaprovecha el valioso tiempo de profesionales que podrían estar agregando más valor a la empresa y mejorando el proceso a un alto nivel en lugar de simplemente sobrevivir. El desperdicio de recursos en el proceso de RH El equipo promedio dedica una cantidad excesiva de tiempo a tareas operativas, manuales y repetitivas. No solo la selección, sino también responder las preguntas repetitivas de los candidatos, recordarles las entrevistas, enviar correos electrónicos de ida y vuelta para programar citas. Además, para muchos equipos, el horario de trabajo no es suficiente y necesitan usar horas extras para cubrir toda la carga de trabajo. Al llegar el fin de semana, la carga de trabajo se duplicará con más solicitantes. La eficiencia en RH y el impacto en los KPIs de la compañía Cuando pensamos en el impacto de las tareas manuales, tal vez solo estemos considerando el agotamiento en los equipos de reclutamiento. Algo que ya es una señal de alerta en nuestra administración de recursos. Sin embargo, los impactos de las tareas manuales pueden ser múltiples: aumento de las horas dedicadas por los reclutadores a un solo candidato, ciclos largos de contratación, falta de métricas y más. Esto eventualmente influye en el negocio, ya que las nóminas incompletas podrían traducirse en menos camareros en una de las tiendas, o ningún cajero. Esto reduce la cantidad de productos que puedes vender o la lentitud con la que puedes atender a un cliente, resultando en clientes insatisfechos y una venta menos o una mala reseña. Al final, pierdes ingresos y clientes. Con esto en mente, podemos comprender que al centrarnos en tareas de alto valor en el proceso de reclutamiento y asegurarnos de que nuestros recursos se utilizan sabiamente, podemos tener un impacto directo en los ingresos, la experiencia de los candidatos y la percepción de la marca. ¿Cómo están resolviendo las compañías la eficiencia y el uso específico de sus recursos limitados? Lo bueno es que es un problema generalizado entre los equipos de reclutamiento. Lo que significa que podemos ver y aprender de cómo otros han resuelto el mismo problema y aprender de sus soluciones. En empresas que hacen contratación masiva de trabajadores de primera línea como Heineken, Oxxo y Nemak en México , el problema se ha abordado principalmente mediante: Automatización Actualización de formularios de aplicación por tecnología más eficiente Estandarización de procesos y actualización de su tecnología. Estas empresas han optado por buscar la herramienta que les permita optimizar y mejorar su proceso. En vez de compartimentar las mejoras en partes específicas o sumar herramientas con soluciones parciales, optaron por encontrar una solución que eficientizara su proceso de punta a punta. Veamos sus resultados: Automatización en Heineken A través de la automatización, los reclutadores de Heineken us ahorraron más de 10,000 horas. Heineken estaba lidiando por mantenerse al día con el flujo de necesidades de contratación en volumen alto debido a las reformas laborales en México en los últimos años . Se enfocaron en adoptar una herramienta que pudiera automatizar la preselección de candidatos. Esto les permitió concentrarse en construir la marca empleadora y actuar en su estrategia de adquisición de talento. La automatización impactó no solo en la eficiencia del equipo, sino también en la reducción del tiempo y los costos del proceso. El beneficio de un proceso más rápido no solo tiene un impacto económico en la empresa, sino que también aumenta la probabilidad de llegar a los mejores candidatos y contratarlos. En la guía para atraer y retener talento en mercados competitivos , se descubrió que el tiempo promedio de contratación es de 34 días, pero los mejores candidatos están fuera del mercado en 10 días. Por lo tanto, la inmediatez de la respuesta y el filtrado son un activo valioso para las empresas que buscan contratar a los mejores candidatos. Actualización de formularios a aplicaciones simples en Oxxo y Nemak En la guía para atraer y retener talento en mercados competitivos , se encontró que para quienes trabajan por hora, el abandono de los solicitantes suele ocurrir en los primeros 3-5 minutos. Por lo tanto, si un trabajo tarda más de 5 minutos en completarse, la tasa de abandono del candidato aumenta al 50%-75%; las solicitudes con más de 25 preguntas tienen una tasa de abandono del 25%-50%. También, se toma en consideración que la mayoría de los candidatos que aplican tienden a preferir procesos de solicitud más rápidos y más sencillos. Por lo tanto, si actualmente estás utilizando formularios, preguntas largas o solicitando un currículum que los candidatos pueden no haber actualizado, posiblemente debas considerar actualizar a una forma de preselección más amigable, rápida y eficiente. En el caso de Heineken, se pensó en el chatbot de IA de Emi para seleccionar y clasificar a los candidatos y programarlos en cuestión de minutos. OXXO adoptó la automatización con AI para reemplazar sus antiguos métodos de aplicación. Hoy en día los candidatos aplican a Oxxo a través de una liga de WhatsApp que cuenta con una preselecciónde IA automatizada 24/7 para filtrar a los aplicantes y agendar la primera entrevista con ellos. Al incorporar la herramienta de Emi a sus equipos, han logrado reducir en un 86% las tiendas que estaban con una reducción crítica de empleados, bajar un 26% sus vacantes disponibles y reducir un 33% el tiempo que les llevaba completar sus nóminas. Nemak también utilizó la automatización y la IA en sus procesos de reclutamiento. Estaban intentando reducir las tareas manuales y subir la productividad y eficiencia en sus equipos de RH. Principalmente mejorando el filtrado de perfiles, el tiempo de respuesta y la captación de documentación. Lograron subir un 54% en su contratación de puestos operativos, contactar al 100% de los candidatos y reducir en un 75% sus costos de outsourcing. Cómo integrar la automatización en tu proceso de reclutamiento Identificar los mayores puntos de dolor y definir KPIs y objetivos Identificar los KPIs y objetivos que se alineen con tu empresa y equipo de reclutamiento te ayudará a enfocarte en encontrar las herramientas adecuadas para ti y las soluciones que mejor te ayuden a alcanzarlos. Investiga, explora y visualiza los resultados que estás tratando de lograr dentro de un año. Esto te ayudará a mantenerte enfocado e identificar los primeros pasos con mayor claridad. Además, identificar tus mayores puntos de dolor actuales te ayudará a iniciar una innovación progresiva que garantice cubrir las prioridades primero. Innovaciones progresivas Los grandes cambios se logran a través de acciones pequeñas. Una vez que identifiques los mayores puntos de mejora y las prioridades de la empresa, puedes comenzar a implementar las mejoras específicas. Es importante tener en cuenta que los cambios llevarán tiempo y requerirán de una buena comunicación y alineamiento entre equipos. Se puede ir mejorando de manera progresiva, adoptando una solución por partes que pueda ayudarnos a poder progresivamente acercarnos al reclutamiento que buscamos. Automatizando la adquisición de talento Hay muchas maneras de mejorar los procesos de reclutamiento. Para aquellas empresas que buscan tener un impacto directo en sus KPIs, además de ayudar a sus equipos de RH a trabajar con mayor eficiencia, recomendaría explorar soluciones completas donde la automatización y uso de la IA pueden maximizar los resultados. Como fue el caso en las empresas líderes como Walmart, Heineken, Oxxo y Nemak . Puedes leer sus casos de éxito completos y solicitar una demo con Emi en caso de buscar explorar el potencial impacto que la automatización puede tener en tu empresa. Para quienes busquen solucionar el problema de manera superficial hasta poder efectuar mejoras de raíz, sugeriría implementaciones graduales en las áreas mencionadas (filtros de candidatos, automatización de tareas manuales y recolección de documentación). En operaciones pequeñas, donde manejan volúmenes de menos de 200 reclutados anualmente, un chatbot y herramientas específicas para sus necesidades pueden servir como solución inicial. Pero si estamos hablando de volúmenes masivos o por encima de 1000, es conveniente utilizar plataformas completas con soluciones integrales. ‍

title: How To Set Effective Objectives & Define Key Results (OKRs)
summary: Examples of well crafted OKR. The characteristics of a good objective. How to cascade OKRs across an organization. Setting effective OKRs. How to make objectives inspiring and motivating.
body_text: How To Set Effective Objectives & Define Key Results (OKRs) OKRs (Objectives and Key Results) inject purpose and clarity into your goals. While the Objective captures what you aspire to accomplish, the Key Results detail how you'll track your progress. But how do you set effective objectives and properly define the key results to achieve your organization's goal? This article breaks down the process of characterizing and setting effective objectives, as well as breaking down the process of creating measurable and achievable key results. What are the Characteristics of a Good Objective? A good objective should typically be Significant, Concrete & Actionable, Inspirational, Timebound and Aligned. Through these characteristics, the objectives can be seen not only to be specific, but doable and they're also aligned with organization’s strategic goals, in turn promoting a motivated and harmonized team effort How to Cascade OKRs Across the Organization It's essential to cascade OKRs from the company level down to departments and individuals to ensure alignment and strategic execution: Company-Level OKRs: Begin with the company's vision and long-term plan (3-5 years). Develop high-level objectives that align with this strategy and define key results to measure progress. Department-Level OKRs: Break down company objectives into department-specific objectives. Each department should have key results that directly support the company objectives, creating a clear link between departmental efforts and overall company goals. Team and Individual-Level OKRs: Further cascade department objectives to teams and individuals. Team objectives should support department goals, and individual objectives should align with team goals. This ensures every team member understands their role in achieving broader organizational objectives. How to Make Objectives Inspiring and Motivating Leaders can create objectives that are not only clear and actionable but also engaging and inspiring in order to drive the team to achieve exceptional results by following these 5 strategies; Align Objectives with Personal and Team Aspirations : Connect the objectives to the personal goals and aspirations of team members. When individuals see how their work contributes to their personal growth and the team's success, they are more likely to feel motivated. Set Ambitious and Impactful Goals : Establish challenging objectives that push the team out of their comfort zones but are still attainable. Be clear to communicate the impact and importance of these goals, so that team members can understand how their efforts contribute to the larger objective and make a difference. Foster a Collaborative and Inclusive Environment : Encourage collaboration and involve team members in the process of setting objectives. When people have a say in the goals they are working towards and feel part of a collective effort, they are more likely to feel a sense of ownership and motivation. Celebrate Progress and Success: Regularly acknowledge and celebrate progress towards objectives. Recognizing achievements, both big and small, can boost morale and keep the team motivated. Maintain Transparency and Accountability: Ensure transparency about the progress towards objectives and hold everyone accountable. Consistently communicate the vision and purpose behind the objectives, reinforcing why the goals are important and how they align with the organization's mission and values. What are Key Results? Key results are defined as specific and measurable outcomes that track the achievement of an objective. They serve as benchmarks to assess progress and determine if the objective has been met. According to the book, Measure What Matters by John Doerr, key results are Specific and time-bound, Measurable and verifiable, Aggressive yet realistic, Result oriented as well as Limited in number. How to Create Measurable and Achievable Key Results Creating measurable and achievable key results that drive meaningful progress towards your objectives is as easy as following the 5 steps below. They include; Start with the Objective : Clearly define the objective you want to achieve. Ensure it is significant, actionable, and inspirational. Identify Success Indicators: Determine what success looks like for this objective. What are the indicators that will show you’ve achieved it? Quantify the Indicators : Turn these indicators into measurable metrics. Ask yourself how you will measure progress and what specific targets will indicate success. Set a Time Frame: Decide on a realistic time frame for achieving these key results. This helps in maintaining focus and urgency. Review and Refine : Ensure that your key results are ambitious but realistic, specific, and measurable. Refine them if necessary to align better with the objective and overall strategy. Considerations for Effective OKRs Connection: Articulate the connection between department and company OKRs, and between individual and department OKRs. Starting Line vs. Finishing Line OKRs: Identify your current position in the journey towards your objectives. Ownership: Ensure clear ownership of OKRs at every level. Each Objective and Key Result should have a single clear owner responsible for them, even if they are not the only one involved in executing the OKR. Focus on Outcome Metrics: Prioritize outcome metrics over outputs/tasks/milestones. For example, instead of setting a key result like "Complete 10 customer calls," set a key result like "Increase customer satisfaction score by 20%”. Limit Objectives: Limit each department/team to no more than three objectives and ensure each objective has no more than three key results. Examples of a Well-crafted Objective and Key Result (OKR) These examples illustrate the key characteristics of good objectives: they are significant, concrete, actionable, inspirational, and time-bound. Here are some examples: Organization: Google Goal: Launch Chrome Browser: Objective : Launch the Chrome browser by Q3 with a focus on speed, simplicity, and security. Key Results: Achieve 20 million users within six months of launch. Obtain a 95% satisfaction rate from users. Ensure compatibility with top 10 web applications. ‍ Organization: Intel Goal: Improve Manufacturing Efficiency: Objective: Enhance manufacturing efficiency to meet the growing demand for microprocessors. Key Results: Increase production yield by 10% within six months. Reduce manufacturing costs by 15% within the fiscal year. Decrease production cycle time from 14 days to 10 days by the end of the quarter. title: Setting Startup Market Valuations Effectively
summary: Understand your market value to fundraise faster and manage dilution.
body_text: Introduction Understanding market valuations for high growth technology companies can feel like deciphering a complex code, but having an understanding of market norms is crucial for any company aiming to secure funding. Market valuations play a crucial role in determining how much your company is worth in the eyes of potential investors, while managing for long term dilution. In this guide, we'll walk you through the essentials of understanding and utilizing market valuations to your advantage. How to Determine Private Market Value First of all, what is market value? Market value refers to the estimated amount for which a company can be sold on the open market. It reflects the value that investors are willing to pay based on perceived potential, financial performance, and market conditions. Determining private market value isn't just about picking a method and sticking to it. Often, a combination of methods provides a more accurate picture: Gather Financial Data An up to date financial projection model will allow you to estimate your cash needs for the next 18-24 months. Allowing you to model out how you would deploy new investment and grow revenue as a result. Analyze Market Conditions Understand the current market trends, investor sentiment, and economic factors that might affect your valuation. At the later stages companies are valued on a multiple of forward looking ARR. At the earlier stages, setting company valuations are based much more on market comparable for that stage, sector, and geography. Manage for Dilution Companies need to manage their dilution when fundraising, in order to preserve enough equity for future rounds of funding. The rule of thumb is to try to only sell around 20% of equity per round. This broken cap table chart from Backing Minds does a great job modeling that out and it well worth a look: Broken Cap Table Chart ‍ Later Stage Company Valuations While there are various ways to calculate market value, here's a basic formula used in the Comparable Company Analysis: Market Value = Share Price × Total Outstanding Shares For private companies, adjustments might be needed to factor in control premiums or liquidity discounts. Bessemer Cloud Index : The Bessemer Cloud Index tracks the Forward Revenue Multiple for later stage companies. Putting aside the boom cycle of 2021, on average the Forward Revenue Multiple sits around 6x. Priced Equity Company Valuations When analyzing market valuations for priced equity rounds, one of my favorite people to follow is Peter Walker. He is the Head of Insights at Carta and is constantly publishing helpful information for founders. Here are he market valuations for Seed, Series A, Series B, and Series C fo the 25th, 50th, and 75th percentiles throughout Q1 2024. Early Stage SAFE & Convertible Company Valuations Peter and the Carta team also published some great Q1 2024 data on early convertible rounds run on SAFE's and Convertible notes. Picking A Valuation For Your Company Picking a valuation for your company is a balancing act between getting 3 things right: Two inputs: Cash Needs: Raising an amount that is enough to execute and hit the milestones you need to hit in 24 months. Valuation : Setting a valuations that fairly values your business, while... And one output: Dilution : ...managing dilution of the company stock so you don't have a broken cap table. ‍ Negotiating Company Valuation With Investors Investors look at deals all day. It's their full time job. So investors are usually very aware of where the market norms are for valuations at each stage of funding. And they are incentivized to pay a low a price as possible for a company, in order to increase their return multiple. It is also important to remember that the investor is often the "market maker" setting the valuation, as they are the one writing the check. But founders only have one company and don't spend all day in the weeds looking at various rounds. And founders are often a "market taker" at earlier stages of funding. This is why familiarizing yourself with anonymized market data can be a powerful way of level the playing field for founders. Having awareness around what are the market norms for valuations in your stage, sector, and geography can help protect founders from being taken advantage of. Deal Rooms and Private Links: Share critical deal information and documents securely, ensuring potential investors have all the necessary data at their fingertips. Investor Database: Leverage Finta's extensive investor database to identify and target the most suitable investors for your fundraising efforts ‍ Final Thoughts ‍ Understanding and leveraging market valuations is both art and science. While confusing at first, get familiar with market norms can significantly impact your fundraising success. By utilizing the right methods and tools, like those offered by Finta, you can navigate this complex process with confidence and precision. Remember, a well-calculated market value not only attracts the right investors, but also sets the stage for sustainable growth and success of your company. title: Top 5 motivos de abandono de carrinho no e-commerce
summary: Descubra os principais motivos de abandono de carrinho no e-commerce e como otimizar a experiência de compra para aumentar as vendas. Agende uma demonstração da Compra Rápida e potencialize seus resultados!
body_text: Quem trabalha com e-commerce sabe o esforço e investimento necessário para trazer clientes ao seu site. Diferente das lojas físicas, onde na maioria dos casos os vendedores promovem uma venda assistida e conseguem auxiliar os clientes com quaisquer dificuldades ou objeções, no e-commerce pequenos obstáculos podem fazer o cliente desistir da compra, e o investimento para trazê-lo vai por água abaixo. Mas dos limões que vem a limonada: como 70% dos carrinhos são abandonados, os sites com uma experiência de compra otimizada e voltada ao cliente conseguem um grande salto na conversão e nas vendas. Um estudo¹ recente perguntou a mais de dois mil usuários as razões para terem abandonado um carrinho nos últimos três meses e vamos destrinchar suas principais causas. Aqui, desconsideramos os usuários que “estavam somente navegando”. Existe um perfil de usuário que gosta de navegar nas páginas de produto e montar carrinhos, mesmo sem a intenção de comprar naquele momento. Apesar de ser uma grande oportunidade, podendo ser atacada com algumas estratégias como ofertas relâmpago e 1-click checkout, isto fica para outro post. Aqui, focaremos nas desistências de clientes já com a intenção de compra. Estudo da Baymard com 2219 usuários. 1) Custos adicionais muito altos Os custos adicionais além do preço dos produtos no checkout são o principal motivo para o abandono do carrinho. Apesar de abaixar o custo de entrega ou oferecer frete grátis para todas as compras sejam estratégias com bons resultados, nem sempre podem ser executadas por afetarem a margem e a lucratividade. Porém, muitas lojas pecam na forma de comunicar as alternativas aos clientes e acabam perdendo vendas por isso. Na maioria das lojas, a possibilidade de frete grátis está atrelada a um valor mínimo de compra, mas nem sempre é comunicada da melhor forma. Este valor mínimo e, mais importante, o valor em produtos que falta para atingir o frete grátis deve estar disponível em diversas etapas da compra. Normalmente, está presente no carrinho, mas quando o cliente está efetivamente tomando a decisão sobre o frete no checkout ela já não aparece mais, e a compra é abandonada. Uma possibilidade interessante é utilizar um order bump para oferecer um produto com o valor faltante: “Adicione este acessório por R$ 39,90 para ganhar o frete grátis”. Por fim, muitas lojas tornam o processo de escolha do frete mais difícil ao não apresentar de forma clara todas as alternativas disponíveis. Em vez de “Frete Empresa Rapidona - 3 dias úteis”, o cliente prefere “Opção Expressa - entregue quinta-feira, dia 7”. A retirada em loja é uma opção omnichannel com crescimento expressivo, normalmente sem custos e com o menor tempo, disponível em minutos ou poucas horas. Porém, estes benefícios raramente são destacados na etapa do frete, com um botão “retirada em loja” discreto ou só disponível na etapa de carrinho. 2) O site queria que eu criasse uma conta Criar uma conta é um processo tedioso e exige um nível maior de confiança do cliente. Com o aumento da preocupação com a privacidade dos dados, podem hesitar em compartilhar algumas informações desnecessárias para o processo de compra. Logicamente existem inúmeros benefícios de coletar mais informações e criar um relacionamento mais próximo com seu cliente, mas condicionar isto ao processo de compra online até para quem não quer impacta significativamente os resultados, enquanto existem alternativas. Neste processo, a necessidade de criação de senhas traz outros problemas. Estamos sujeitos a gerenciar senhas para inúmeros sites e é difícil manter um padrão simples, tanto por segurança como pelos diferentes requisitos exigidos por cada site. Inevitavelmente, as senhas são esquecidas e é necessário recuperá-las pelo e-mail, processo com uma taxa de abandono de aproximadamente 20%. 3) Entrega muito demorada Uma desvantagem do e-commerce em relação às lojas físicas é a demora entre a compra e o momento de usufruir do produto, especialmente quando seu uso seria em um evento, festa ou viagem. A oferta de opções expressas de entrega, embora mais caras, dá mais possibilidades ao cliente e ajuda a diminuir o abandono. Vale destacar novamente a boa comunicação da retirada em loja quando disponível, idealmente com a sinalização da loja mais perto do CEP informado. 4) Eu não confiei os dados os dados do meu cartão ao site Infelizmente, ainda existe muita desconfiança no processo de compra online e o grande número de fraudes prejudica tanto os clientes como os varejistas. A confiança do cliente depende muito da força da marca, e opções para as lojas emergentes são o uso de certificados e parceria com outras marcas relevantes, como subadquirentes ou plataformas. No Brasil, o PIX é uma alternativa aos cartões percebida como mais segura por parte dos usuários. 5) Processo de checkout muito longo/complicado Querendo ou não, cerca de 75% do e-commerce no Brasil é dominado pelos quatro maiores marketplaces e provavelmente o seu produto ou um substituto está lá com um preço competitivo. Segundo nossas entrevistas com usuários, mais de 30% dos clientes preferem pagar até 15% mais caro e comprar com um click no marketplace onde já tem cadastro em vez de se registrar em um site novo. Por isso, é extremamente importante oferecer um checkout rápido e com poucas etapas para evitar a desistência. Conclusão Diferente de navegar nas páginas de produto, o processo de checkout pode ser tedioso e até frustrante, e diferentes obstáculos resultam na alta desistência de compras. Não é só o valor da compra perdido, mas a oportunidade de fidelizar um cliente e todo o seu lifetime value está em risco. Por isso, vale a pena investir numa experiência de checkout rápida e intuitiva. Alguns pontos, como o tempo e o custo do frete, nem sempre conseguimos alterar por questões de margem, mas a forma de apresentar e comunicar ao cliente tem grande impacto na conversão. Por fim, é extremamente importante conversar com os seus clientes e entender quais os principais motivos de abandono no seu site, e atuar especificamente neles. Não é fácil e a maioria das plataformas não são flexíveis para alterar a experiência. Na Compra Rápida, somos experts em checkout e estudamos todos os dias como cada etapa pode ser aprimorada para uma melhor experiência e maior conversão. Além disso, todas as pessoas que compraram com Compra Rápida podem comprar com 1 click de forma segura em um site da rede, mesmo se for sua primeira vez nele. ¹ Baymard, 2023

title: GraphOS Summer 2024 Launch Recap
body_text: On, June 12, 2024, we hosted our GraphOS summer launch event , where we announced new features designed to improve the performance and operational excellence of GraphQL platforms. These new capabilities improve how API platform teams implement and optimize GraphQL federation, providing faster baseline performance and greater control over API request execution in a supergraph. GraphQL Federation: Usage on the rise GraphQL adoption in the enterprise is at an inflection point, driven by the proliferation of federated GraphQL architectures – a pattern originally introduced by Apollo GraphQL in 2019 with the launch of Apollo Federation and GraphOS . In a recent report , Gartner® predicts that 30% of enterprises using GraphQL will utilize GraphQL federation by 2027, up from less than 5% in 2024. Apollo believes this trend suggests the number of enterprises using GraphQL federation as their API access layer will increase by 12x. Apollo Federation is a specification for modularly and declaratively mapping existing application services into a unified GraphQL API access layer, known as a supergraph. This architecture empowers platform engineering teams to provide client applications with self-serve access to services through a single GraphQL endpoint, facilitating the rapid evolution of complex end-user experiences. By decoupling backend development from frontend complexity, teams can independently manage and contribute services to the supergraph via subgraphs, representing core business entities such as Product, User, or Cart. In our summer launch, we focused on the Operational Excellence pillar of the Supergraph Architecture Framework . The Operational Excellence pillar focuses on empowering subgraph and stewardship teams. A well-architected graph isn’t only technically excellent—it’s also operationally excellent. Processes and tools should be in place to ensure that the supergraph is easy to use, understand, and maintain. These principles help ensure that the graph is a successful tool for building new experiences quickly. Key Announcements Query Batching: GA GraphOS now supports end-to-end (client-to-subgraph) query batching , which is essential for ensuring consistency in component-based architecture where individual micro-frontends (MFE) make requests separately to fetch data relevant to them. By handling several queries in one request, this feature has the additional performance benefit of reduced network traffic and server load. Enhanced Telemetry and Insights: GA The enhancements to custom telemetry in GraphOS Router provide platform teams with deeper visibility into the performance of their supergraphs. New support for custom events gives you full customization over signalling when something of note happens in the Apollo Router’s request lifecycle. New custom instruments collects custom data and reports measurements to a metric backend. Combined, enhanced telemetry allows client teams to investigate runtime errors and performance issues autonomously, reducing the debugging burden on core platform teams. Additionally, GraphOS Studio now offers more comprehensive checks and insights , giving teams greater control over supergraph operation validation to mitigate production errors. Entity Caching with Per-Subgraph TTL: Public Preview Configuring response caching in a supergraph can be challenging due to the varied refresh rates of different fields. Subgraph entity caching addresses this by allowing platform teams to cache entities centrally while setting granular TTLs for each subgraph. For example, a Product entity can have a long TTL for its Name field and a short TTL for its Inventory field, so long as they are resolved by different subgraphs. Demand Control: Public Preview Platform teams often need to protect their graphs against highly complex queries that can cause service disruption if left unchecked. Our new native cost calculation and limiting features make it easier for teams to observe the average cost of operations in their graph and implement cost controls centrally to avoid misuse of their GraphQL endpoints. Transforming API Platform Operations These new features mark a significant step forward in how organizations can improve the operational excellence with which they manage federated GraphQL architectures. By providing advanced tools for caching, cost control, and query batching, Apollo GraphOS empowers platform teams to build, operate, and evolve supergraphs efficiently. To learn more about these features and more, including schema visualization, context directives, and checks and insights, watch the Summer Launch webinar hosted by VP Product, Rob Brazier. Written by Andrew I. Carlson Read more by Andrew I. Carlson

title: VC Industry Outlook 2024: Navigating the New Venture Landscape with Allocate
summary: Allocate recently pooled nearly 100 venture GPs and LPs on what they see as major trends in 2024.
body_text: Introduction As we approach 2024, the venture capital industry stands at a crossroads of challenges and opportunities. The "VC Industry Outlook 2024" by Allocate sheds light on the predictions that will shape the future of investing. Let's delve into a quick summary of the insights and forecasts that will inform the strategies of investors and entrepreneurs alike. The link to the full report is available at the bottom. ‍ Industry Opportunities Emergence of new, capital-efficient startups pre-Series B, with a spotlight on generative AI sectors. Mega-cap funds shifting investment focus to later stages with more measurable metrics. Specialist seed funds poised to lead inception rounds. Industry Challenges Consolidation within VC firms and the possibility of partner exits. Seed stage markets predicted to consolidate by up to 50%. Shift in investment strategies to prioritize earnings potential and positive margins. Venture Firm Dynamics Market reset creating a divide based on firms' competitive advantages. VCs facing fundraising challenges may pivot to focus on existing portfolios. Enhanced use of AI for investment activity efficiency. Early Stage Dynamics Rise of a new breed of capital-efficient startups focused on sustainable growth. Seed funds expected to have a strong year, with "boring businesses" transformed by AI. Artificial Intelligence AI expected to drive significant productivity gains, despite data and monetization challenges. Emerging diverse founder backgrounds challenge traditional VC evaluation metrics. Deep tech AI startups to potentially lead to a surge in unicorns. What Will Limited Partners Do? LPs reassessing commitments, with a lean towards smaller, proven early-stage funds. Significant venture capital allocation anticipated from the wealth channel. Emphasis on funds with consistent DPI and disciplined fund size and strategy. Mergers and Acquisitions Increased M&A activity expected due to resets in company valuations and end-of-runway scenarios. High-profile startups may resort to shutdowns or engage in nominal M&A deals. Sector-Focused Thoughts Anticipated collaboration surge between biotech and pharma companies. Growth in climate-tech investments and AI consumer device integration. Predicted consumer market revitalization, with innovative products leading the way. Startup Fundraising Founders and investors alike have refocused on capital efficiency with slower and more durable growth, which may reduce downstream funding in the short term. While this reset is expected to be positive for returns overall, it could protract the time to exit for many companies who are growing more gradually. Founders expected to prioritize capital efficiency, with potential slow-down in funding cycles. Emergence of profit-sharing tech startups as a response to challenging fundraising conditions. Rise of Capital Light startups, bridging the gap between traditional funding models. Views on Liquidity Alternative liquidity paths such as secondaries or small-cap IPOs gaining traction due to a tough exit environment. Regulatory focus and profitability becoming central to the venture liquidity narrative in 2024. Conclusion The venture capital landscape in 2024 appears to be a mosaic of evolving strategies and newfound efficiencies. With AI's disruptive influence and changing financial dynamics, adaptability remains key. Investors and founders must navigate this terrain with an eye for sustainable growth and a strategic approach to capital deployment. ‍ Read the full report by Allocate here .

title: Top 5 Hurco CNC Machinist Blogs

body_text: Hurco Senior Product Technical Specialist Mike Cope has been writing the Hurco CNC Machinist Blog for years. It covers everything from control features to mounting configurations to comparing different styles of machines. Several articles have become quite popular. Here are the top five most viewed Hurco CNC Machinist Blog posts over the last year: CNC TURRET DRIVE TOOL MOUNTING CONFIGURATIONS: BMT VS VDI Previously, I (Mike Cope) published a two-part series on the basics of mill-turn technology, where I cover topics such as: axis configurations , the orientation of live tooling holders , mill-turn terminology, instances when a Y-axis might be necessary, etc. In this article, I discuss the differences between the driven tool mounting configurations and offer our opinion on the benefits and challenges associated with each. READ BLOG ROTARY BROACH: HOW TO DRILL A SQUARE HOLE Is it possible to drill a square hole? Many will snicker at this age-old question and say, “Of course you can’t drill a square hole!” Well, it turns out you most certainly can drill a square hole… and a rectangular hole, and a hexagon shaped hole, a hole with splines, double keyways — the list goes on and on! READ BLOG 5-AXIS CNC PROGRAMMING: ROTARY ANGLES OR TOOL VECTORS? When programming in 5-axis , we have two distinct options that we can use to command rotary moves and positions. We can output the data using either rotary angles or tool vectors. Although each one has its pros and cons, I (Mike Cope) prefer to configure a postprocessor to output these rotary commands as IJK tool vectors, instead of the more common ABC-axis rotary angles. In this article, I (Mike Cope) will shine some light on the basics of live-tool machining and the application of the optional Y-axis. title: Innovate or Stagnate
summary: innovate-or-stagnate
body_text: In an era where technological advancements are continuously reshaping patient expectations and treatment standards, orthodontic practices face a critical choice: to innovate or risk stagnation. The introduction of 3D printed aligners into the orthodontic industry has not only revolutionized treatment methodologies but also presented a unique opportunity for practices to distinguish themselves in a crowded marketplace. This blog post delves into the competitive edge that 3D printed aligners can provide and how embracing this technology can propel orthodontic practices to the forefront of the industry. ### Embracing Cutting-Edge Technology The move towards 3D printing aligners in-house signifies more than just an operational shift; it reflects a commitment to embracing the latest technological advancements. Patients today are more informed and have higher expectations regarding their treatment options. They seek providers that offer the most advanced, efficient, and customized care possible. By incorporating 3D printing technology into their services, orthodontists can meet these demands head-on, offering precise, tailored treatments that align with modern expectations of medical care. ### Enhancing Practice Reputation Utilizing 3D printing for aligner production positions an orthodontic practice as a leader in innovation within the dental community. This not only elevates the practice's reputation among peers but also makes it more attractive to prospective patients. In a digital age where social proof is paramount, the ability to showcase advanced technology and successful treatment outcomes directly on platforms such as Instagram or Facebook can significantly enhance a practice's visibility and appeal. ### Differentiation in a Competitive Market The dental care market, particularly within orthodontics, is exceedingly competitive. Practices that offer unique services or employ novel technologies have a distinct advantage. 3D printed aligners provide such an edge by differentiating a practice through the promise of faster, more efficient, and customizable treatments. This differentiation is not just about the technology itself but about the patient-centric approach it embodies, emphasizing personalized care and innovation. ### Accelerated Treatment Processes One of the key competitive advantages of 3D printed aligners is the significant reduction in turnaround times. Traditional methods often involve waiting for aligners to be produced and shipped by an external provider, a process that can take weeks. With in-house 3D printing, aligners can be produced in a matter of hours, allowing patients to start their treatment sooner. This efficiency not only improves patient satisfaction but also allows orthodontists to manage their caseloads more effectively, potentially increasing the number of patients they can treat. ### Cost Efficiency and Patient Affordability While the initial investment in 3D printing technology may be significant, the long-term cost savings for practices are considerable. By reducing the need for external manufacturing, practices can lower production costs and, in turn, offer more competitive pricing to their patients. This cost efficiency can be a critical deciding factor for patients choosing between orthodontic providers, making 3D printed aligners a financially attractive option for both practices and their patients. ### Conclusion The integration of 3D printed aligners into orthodontic practice is more than just an operational upgrade; it's a strategic move towards future-proofing your business. By adopting this innovative technology, orthodontists can enhance their competitive edge, improve patient outcomes, and secure a leading position in the rapidly evolving dental care industry. As we move forward, the choice for orthodontic practices will become increasingly clear: innovate with 3D printing technology or risk being left behind in the wake of progress. ‍
